title: Chapter X

teacherSummary.text: On the glacier Montanvert, the creature approaches. Victor curses it; the creature answers eloquently, reminding Victor of his duties: 'I ought to be thy Adam, but I am rather the fallen angel.' He asks Victor to hear his story, and Victor follows him to a hut.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend. Make me happy, and I shall again be virtuous” slowly and put it in my own words: The creature tells Victor he was kind and good, misery made him a fiend, and happiness would make him virtuous again. Next, craft. I notice the antithesis of "benevolent and good" against "fiend," and the cause-and-effect turn on "made." The strongest word is “misery”: it is the cause he blames for his change, placing responsibility on how he was treated. Then, effect. What argument does the creature make about how he became evil? My answer: The creature argues that he became evil because rejection and misery made him so, not his nature; he demands that Victor, as his maker, take responsibility, which makes us question who the real monster is.
